description:
An always-on desktop app of autonomous AI employees that work inside your IM chats

Autonomous AI employees, on the job. Embedded where you and your teammates already work, it starts the moment a need appears and carries the task through to delivery.
- A teammate in the IM chat — after a long thread, just @ it with "turn this into a plan", waker already knows what just happened.
- Autonomously start work on its own — IM messages, schedules, hook events, or API calls, any of these four can trigger it started.
- Multiple wakers, working together — one task, split across roles: they work in parallel, hand off as needed, and review each other — fully traceable.
Three underlying systems let them get real work done on the front line:
- Harness engineering for stable delivery — task state persists, failures recover, and critical steps come with verification and retry. Work spanning hours or days keeps moving toward the goal.
- Your first AI employee — every AI employee has a name, a role, an onboarding date, scoped permissions, and a traceable record. Review what it did and how well it delivered, just like any team member.
- Job skills continuously expand — the built-in role skill library supports custom skills, so digital employee capabilities extend continuously with your needs.
- Acts inside your existing workflows — it works right inside group chats, approvals, docs, sheets, and internal systems, never crossing its permission boundaries.
- Customize for each profession — systematically built for each role: skills, methods, and judgment. Not a generic model wearing a role-shaped prompt.
- Knowledge retention and continuous evolution — you can view, correct, or forget any memory, letting your digital employee forget faulty context. Every collaboration builds shared knowledge.
- Secure, governable, accountable — each role gets its own identity and least-privilege access; sensitive actions require approval and critical actions are fully logged, so automation never crosses your enterprise boundary.
Feishu Personal Avatars and More Reliable Group Tasks
What's New
- Feishu Support for Personal Avatars: Connect your personal Feishu account and select authorized direct chats, group chats, and meeting notes to create your Personal Avatar.
Improvements
- History Recall in Direct Chats: In IM direct chats, look up past tasks and discussions you participated in, along with your own group-member memories, within the same connection and identity scope. Results identify their sources.
- Learning by Date Range: Personal Avatars can search for and learn additional chat and meeting materials within a selected date range.
- Automatic Read Receipts: Enable or disable automatic read receipts in your DingTalk Personal Avatar profile. Replies continue to work when this setting is disabled.
- Memory Search: Improves keyword and semantic search, pagination, and source descriptions while reducing repeated reads for more efficient historical memory queries.
- Response Target Configuration: Improves loading, grouping, and scrolling for group response targets so a slow-loading group does not block the entire list.
Bug Fixes
- Fixed concurrent Windows group tasks failing to start when runtime resources could not be replaced, and some model configuration conflicts preventing task startup.
- Fixed long-running tasks timing out despite ongoing progress, and group tasks failing to resume after being forcibly stopped.
- Fixed empty group Skill lists, failures to reuse resources after download links expired, and faulty plugins affecting menus and references for otherwise healthy Skills.
- Fixed DingTalk image and file uploads and group image reads, and WeCom task results and attachments failing to return to the original conversation.
- Fixed proactive response learning deriving policies from requests belonging to another identity or from the bot's own messages.
- Fixed compatibility with some Connector URLs and tool recovery after upgrades, and scheduling compatibility for existing scheduled tasks.
- Fixed unread-state synchronization for group mentions, the task board, and IM task details, along with name display in WeCom conversations.
